contract.status: PB1 neutral contract; planned experimental work; not ratified; not part of Brontide Base

purpose: One versioned Component contract established before any provider effect. It replaces the two divergent manifest encodings that PB0 inventoried (Cooling v2 and Catalog v1) with a single neutral form.

annotation.purpose: A published contract document may carry documentation beside the contract it declares: which Shape version is additive over which, why another is not, what role an encoding-edge Shape plays. That information is machine-readable and worth keeping adjacent to what it describes. But 'fields' below is exhaustive and unknownFieldPolicy is 'reject', so without a declared mechanism a faithful transcode of such a document is a malformed contract.
annotation.mechanism: A document carrying annotation declares 'annotationFields': the names in it that document rather than declare. A consumer transcoding the document to the wire form drops those names wherever they occur, at any nesting depth, and validates what remains against 'fields'.

artifactEnvelope.rule: Four further names are dropped, at the document root only, because they describe the artifact rather than the contract it declares.
artifactEnvelope.rootOnly: These are dropped only at the root. The same name nested inside the contract data is contract data, and is kept or rejected on its own merits.

rules: A name not listed in 'annotationFields' and not one of the four root envelope names is contract data. A new annotation that does not declare itself therefore becomes 'malformed-message' at the first consumer that transcodes the document, rather than being silently tolerated.
No name in 'annotationFields' may equal a field this schema declares. Annotation may not shadow contract data.
An empty 'annotationFields' declares that the document carries no annotation beyond the root envelope. That is a positive statement, not the same as omitting the member.
Dropping is by name, not by position, so a name declared as annotation is annotation everywhere below the root.
annotation.whyItIsDeclaredHere: PB5 finding, ruled on as Decision 6 in binding/portable/open-decisions.md and recorded 2026-07-28. Both stacks hand-wrote their contracts from the fixture files and dropped the annotations by eye, so neither had ever transcoded one and neither discovered the conflict. The implementation-neutral provider was the first consumer to read a fixture as published, and could not use it. The mechanism lives here, rather than only in each fixture, so that an implementer working from schemas/ alone learns the rule instead of having to infer it from a fixture.

fields.name: contractVersion
fields.rule: Must equal 1 for this contract revision. Any other value is 'unsupported-version'.

provision.purpose: What this Component offers. PB0 recorded no explicit provision or requirement vocabulary in either experiment; this is its first neutral definition.

requirement.purpose: What this Component needs from its peer.

strengthSemantics.required: Negotiation fails closed with 'unsupported-contract' unless the peer provides an exactly matching provision.
strengthSemantics.preferred: Negotiation succeeds without it, and the absence is recorded as a C9 selection reason.
strengthSemantics.optional: Negotiation succeeds without it and the absence is unremarkable.
strengthSemantics.opposed: Negotiation fails closed with 'unsupported-contract' if the peer provides it.

fields.name: detailShape
fields.rule: The Shape of a shaped failed Outcome. It is required because a semantic failure must be shaped rather than exception-borne.

fields.name: resourceFlavors
fields.rule: Declared referenced-resource flavors this Operation accepts; empty means inline payloads only.

operation.normalizes: Cooling declares inputShape and outputShape with a separate details Shape reachable only through the failure path; Catalog declares inputShape and outputShape with no detail Shape at all. The neutral contract names all three positions explicitly.

fields.name: fragmentPolicy
fields.rule: Required when kind is 'record'; forbidden otherwise.

fields.name: fields
fields.rule: Required when kind is 'record'; forbidden otherwise.

fields.name: itemShape
fields.rule: Required when kind is 'sequence'; forbidden otherwise.

fields.name: alternatives
fields.rule: Required when kind is 'choice'; forbidden otherwise.

fields.name: scalar
fields.rule: Required when kind is 'scalar'; names a Shape floor scalar.

fields.name: name
fields.rule: Portable member-token profile [A-Za-z0-9_-]+, unique within the Shape.

order: Validate the contract document structurally; a malformed document is 'malformed-message'.
Compare the provider by exact reference equality; a mismatch is 'unsupported-contract'.
Match every 'required' requirement against an exactly equal peer provision; a miss is 'unsupported-contract'.
Reject any 'opposed' requirement the peer provides; a hit is 'unsupported-contract'.
Compare each negotiated Operation's inputShape, resultShape, detailShape, and requiredFragments for exact equality; a difference is 'unsupported-contract'.
Resolve the authority presentation mode; an unsatisfiable mode is 'invalid-authority-presentation'.
Resolve the representation and resource flavors; an unsupported one is 'unsupported-contract'.
Resolve limits and lifecycle features; an unsupported required feature is 'unsupported-contract'.
Only then assign binding-scoped compact identifiers and freeze the Binding Plan.
negotiation.failClosedRule: Every step above completes before any provider activation. A failure at any step produces zero provider effects.
negotiation.exactnessRule: Version 0.1 negotiates by exact reference equality. There is no structural similarity matching, no nearest-version selection, and no inference of authority from provider availability.
negotiation.providerIdentityRule: A required document naming a provider is binding, not expectational: the peer must answer as that provider or negotiation refuses. Version 0.1 defines no way to say 'any provider of this Component'; an absent or wildcard provider is deliberately undefined and would be an additive change. Because a mismatch is refused, the required and offered providers are equal whenever a plan exists, so the Binding Plan's provider facts are read from the offered document to say who answered rather than who was asked. See open-decisions.md Decision 11.

unknownHandling.what: an unknown Shape, Fragment, or dependency reference
an unknown value in a declared enumeration
